name: Alkaline water / alkaline diet

lead: The alkaline diet and alkaline water rest on the idea that what you eat or drink shifts body pH and thereby health. The diet favours plants and excludes most animal foods and grains.
Reviews report no evidence that diet changes blood pH in healthy people, and no appearance studies were found.

paras: Proponents say foods leave acidic or alkaline residues that affect the body; physiologists note blood pH is tightly regulated, and urine pH does not reflect body acidity.
Excluding food groups can cause nutrient deficiencies, and cancer organisations caution against relying on it; promoters often sell supplements and equipment.

lead: The alkaline diet is a group of loosely related diets based on the idea that foods change the body's pH and that this affects disease. It favours most fruit and vegetables and excludes most grains, meat, cheese and eggs. Alkaline water, often made with ionizer machines, is marketed on a similar premise [1][2].

Proponents have promoted these for energy, weight loss and disease prevention. Reviews and professional bodies report that diet does not meaningfully change blood pH in healthy people, which is tightly regulated between 7.35 and 7.45 [1].

paras: In the 1800s Claude Bernard observed that rabbits switched from plants to meat produced more acidic urine, and later researchers burned foods and measured leftover ash, leading to the 'dietary ash hypothesis'. Alkaline diets were historically used to prevent kidney stones and urinary infections [1].

Marketers of ionized water say it can slow aging, offset acidic foods or hydrate better after exercise [2]. A 2013 review by Hanley and Whiting found no evidence that diet changes blood pH or bicarbonate in healthy people, and urine pH is reported not to reflect overall body acidity [1]. A systematic review in BMJ Open found no link between dietary acid load, alkaline water and cancer, and several cancer organisations reject the cancer claim [2].

The Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics said parts of the diet such as eating green leafy vegetables are likely healthy, while the British Dietetic Association criticised it in 2018 [1]. Excluding food groups can risk nutrient deficiencies, and cancer patients are cautioned about extreme diets [1].
No studies found testing alkaline water or the alkaline diet for appearance outcomes. Reviews of blood pH and cancer are described above [1][2].
